1.point: Sleep and death are not a going-away; the chapter will show which worlds the soul lives in, how it moves between them and how deeds shape it there, so that what it becomes is in our hands.
steps: Open with the prayer's image: neglect is a sleep, waking is knowing God's generosity; sleep set beside the meeting with God.
The tradition pairs sleep with death; at the graveside we say the dead are in barzakh and picture a distant waiting room.
Overturn the picture (the dead go nowhere) and announce the chapter's three steps and its conclusion.

2.point: The three worlds are three depths of one world, so the dead in barzakh have gone deeper, not away.
steps: The soul is a copy of creation; its three ways of knowing each sample one world.
Senses: the material world; the other two are unseen because unperceived, not because distant.
Imagination: a sample of the world of images, which has shape and colour without matter and exists in its own right.
Intellect: a sample of the world of intellects, pure meaning, home of the angels.
The world of images stands between the other two and is therefore called barzakh.
None is a place; each is a deeper dimension of the world we are in.
So the dead in barzakh are in a deeper dimension of this world, and the resurrection is deeper still.

3.point: The soul moves between the worlds, and how far it goes is settled by the life it lives, not fixed at creation.
steps: The soul has a share in each world because it was made to stand between spirit and clay.
The body holds its attention now; the hold loosens in sleep, at death and in contemplation.
Sleep: the soul touches the world of images (dreams that show the future).
Death: the Qur'an pairs it with sleep; the difference is degree; the soul goes on in the image body it already had.
Contemplation: muraqaba turns attention and lets one see into the middle world.
Contrast: angels have fixed stations and cannot move.
The human soul has no fixed station; how far it goes depends on the life it lives.

4.point: Our deeds now are shaping the image body we will meet after death.
steps: Objection: if everyone passes to the middle world, deeds seem to matter little; but habit shows repeated acts shape the self.
The shaping shows faintly on the face here; the image body is far more sensitive to it.
Authority: each person has a second, invisible form determined by the soul's qualities, fixed by its state at death.
Reward and punishment are the deeds themselves made manifest; the light of the faithful is their own.
So the form met after death is one's own deeds; it is being shaped now.

5.point: The self is one, passes through three states from commanding evil to peace, and known acts move it, so what it becomes is in our hands.
steps: If deeds shape the soul, the self is not fixed; the Qur'an names three states.
First state: the self that commands to evil, pulled by pleasure and by worry.
Second state: the self that blames itself, a hopeful sign.
Third state: the self at peace.
These are one self under different names; change the attitude and the state changes.
What moves it: remembrance, fasting and night prayer, which loosen the tie to the body.
They work because the soul takes habits quickly and is elastic; it is entrusted to us, so what it becomes is ours to decide.

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: Hook: explains the prayer and sets sleep beside the meeting with God, the image the chapter turns on.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Moves from sleep to death to barzakh and states the common 'waiting room' picture that the chapter will overturn.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Overturns the picture with the lecturer's claim, gives the reason (the soul) and lays out the three steps and the conclusion.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Supplies the method: the soul is a copy of creation, so each of three ways of knowing samples one world.

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: First world via the senses; also plants the key distinction that 'unseen' means unperceived, not far away.

¶6.label: support
¶6.why: Examples (picturing a face, dreaming) that ¶7 relies on to describe the world of images as shape without matter.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Second world via imagination, with the needed distinction that it exists in its own right.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: Third world via the intellect; also places the angels there, which ¶19 uses.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Puts the world of images between the other two and names it barzakh, the link ¶11 needs to identify the dead's barzakh with the world of images.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: The decisive step: the worlds are dimensions in depth, not places at a distance.

¶11.label: advance
¶11.why: Applies ¶9 and ¶10 to the graveside and extends it to the resurrection; this is where the section's conclusion lands.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Establishes that the soul has a share in each world because it stands between spirit and clay, with a counterpart in the world of images.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Frames the mechanism (attention held by the body) and names the three loosenings the section will walk through.

¶14.label: advance
¶14.why: First loosening, sleep; the prophetic dream shows the soul reaching the middle world.

¶15.label: support
¶15.why: A one-sentence bridge introducing the verse that ¶16 reads; the sleep-death pairing itself was made in ¶1-2, so it could be folded into ¶16.

¶16.label: advance
¶16.why: Second loosening, death: sleep and death differ in degree, and the soul moves to the image body.

¶17.label: support
¶17.why: Deepens the death step (soul carries body; image body was present all along in another dimension), which Section 4 relies on when it says the image body is being shaped now.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: Third loosening, contemplation through muraqaba, with the distinction between the mystics' gift and the Imams' power.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: Gathers the three into 'a soul that moves' and sets up the contrast with angels fixed in station.

¶20.label: advance
¶20.why: Completes the contrast: the human soul has no fixed station and its reach is settled by the life it lives; the point lands.

¶21.label: advance
¶21.why: Raises the objection and answers it with habit shaping the self, using the lying example.

¶22.label: advance
¶22.why: Carries shaping from the face here to the image body, which sin deforms and piety lights; it states much of the conclusion early, so ¶26 must add rather than repeat.

¶23.label: support
¶23.why: Authority for ¶22's claim: a second form determined by the soul's qualities and fixed at the moment of death; introduces the al-Naba' verse.

¶24.label: restate
¶24.why: Its claim, that on that day people appear as their true natures, is already made in ¶23; the bug-to-angel range repeats ¶20. Only its last sentence, leading into the al-Hadid verse, does work for ¶25.

¶25.label: advance
¶25.why: Supplies the mechanism the point needs: the light is the believers' own, and reward and punishment are the deeds themselves made manifest.

¶26.label: advance
¶26.why: Draws the inference from ¶25 to the image body: the form met after death is one's own deeds, being shaped now. Its last sentence repeats ¶22 and could go.

¶27.label: advance
¶27.why: Opens the section's logic (deeds shape the soul, so the self is not fixed) and gives the first state.

¶28.label: support
¶28.why: Reads the Yusuf verse and adds worry as a second pull binding soul to body; ¶35 picks up 'trained to worry about the body'.

¶29.label: advance
¶29.why: Second state, self-blame as a hopeful sign of held values.

¶30.label: advance
¶30.why: Third state, the self at peace, and the route from self-blame to it. Its first sentence repeats ¶29's 'hopeful sign'.

¶31.label: advance
¶31.why: The hinge of the section: the three are one self under different names, so changing the attitude changes the state.

¶32.label: advance
¶32.why: Begins what moves the self: remembrance of God, introducing the al-Ra'd verse.

¶33.label: support
¶33.why: Reads the verse so that its 'rest' is the peace of the third state; ¶32's step needs this to close.

¶34.label: advance
¶34.why: Second set of means, fasting and night prayer, tied to the loosening mechanism from Section 3.

¶35.label: advance
¶35.why: Explains why the acts work (habit, the elastic soul) and delivers the entrustment that makes the outcome ours; the point lands.

¶36.label: restate
¶36.why: Summarises the whole chapter section by section; every claim has already been made and the conclusion was stated in ¶35.

¶37.label: aside
¶37.why: A closing question the chapter does not answer; it serves the next chapter, not this section's point.
